findings.title: The provenance correction note cites an obsolete diagnostic checksum
findings.rationale: Evidence: cp63-web-build-provenance.md:7 identifies the JSON with SHA-256 79f77613a4f804a0ca25181e614159b771b1a2b3aa0ca98a8d719f03f52f0e1f. The actual terminal cp63-web-build-provenance.json hashes to 73d7ac9d0d1e8eb1f4456a8003d6205ed27066b3248da990e9fe4a0ccfa561a9, matching the root's terminal supplement; its line 38 carries the important qualification of the original candidate boolean. The Markdown file's own supplied hash matches, so this is a stale embedded reference rather than a read mismatch. Why now: the note is being admitted as the correction that prevents an unsupported exact-base provenance claim; following its checksum cannot validate the actual corrected evidence. The JSON qualification itself is sound, and no product, layout, security or build defect follows from this reference error.
findings.suggested_action: Correct the note's JSON reference to the actual terminal checksum, or append an explicit hash-bound erratum if preserving the already-dispatched note as immutable evidence. Keep the malformed preparation record and original candidate artifact intact, and retain the limitation that exact pre/post Node local-ID equality and a resolved build-log digest were not proven. Refresh the note/receipt hash in the final evidence index. No source edit, image rebuild, test rerun, new base pin or expanded scope is required for this correction.
